evals.prompt: Run an architecture review of the iOS app in ~/Documents/git/knmi-app-ios (current checkout).
evals.expected_output: Known architecture facts to find: TCA in one local package with about 50-60 modules; MainFeature.swift (about 1,170 lines) and AppRemoteConfigClient.swift as top hot spots; iOS 15 minimum driving Backport, Perception, NavigationStackBackport, and LegacyIntents; branch-pinned forks; unbuildable macOS, tvOS, and watchOS targets; GridDefinition logic duplicated in Swift and the Kotlin Multiplatform framework. Follows the review-architecture method (churn first, evidence per finding, High/Medium/Low, roadmap) and adds iOS depth: reads project instructions; names the architecture from code per the company architecture reference (TCA or MVVM + Coordinators) and judges against it instead of a generic Domain/Application/Infrastructure layering; analyzes the Swift module graph mechanically (Package.swift targets, app target links, import statements) for cycles, wrong-direction and undeclared imports; checks iOS platform health (deployment targets, Swift language mode and strict concurrency, backport code, branch-pinned packages, lockfile drift) without inventing support dates; excludes generated code, .build, and DerivedData; writes one untracked report to docs/ and summarizes in chat; edits no source and changes no git state.
